text:
maria: FYI I pushed a staging dashboard for token-level latency breakdown + per-pool headroom. PTAL: https://staging.redwood.internal/dash/rlatency-pph
kevin: nice, quick glance shows a bump in kernel-selection time around seq_len=512 for pool-3 :thinking_face:
sachin: can you dump the profiler for one of those requests? curious if KV cache misses are contributing
maria: pasted a tiny flamegraph excerpt from the profiler run (trimmed):

```
--- flamegraph ---
render_token -> 45%
  kernel_selector -> 22%
    int8_kernel_fallback -> 12%
  kv_cache_lookup -> 18%
  batching_scheduler -> 10%
  io_wait -> 5%
```

maria: looks like kernel_selector+kv_cache is ~40% of token time for that sample
kevin: that matches the dashboard spike. On the kernel side we saw fallback from avx_fused to generic_int8 when batch_size < 4 and seq_len >= 512
olivia: can we add a small panel that shows "kernel choice by seq_len / batch"? This would help ops correlate model/runtime thresholds
sachin: also add KV cache hit ratio by route. I suspect multi-tenant routes with hot prefixes are thrashing the shared per-pool cache
observability-bot: alert: pool-3 noisy-neighbor score crossed 0.7 at 10:22 UTC — triggered by increased variance in token p95 across routes
maria: created 2 quick panels: kernel_choice_heatmap and per_route_kv_hit. Pushed commit in PR #3124: https://git.redwood/infra/dashboards/pull/3124
kevin: running synthetic test hitting route=chat-short and route=chat-long for pool-3 to reproduce. command:
```
loadtest --pool pool-3 --routes chat-short,chat-long --seq 64,512 --concurrency 20 --duration 5m
```
kevin: initial run shows chat-long p95 token latency up 30% compared to baseline, and KV cache hit ratio dropped from 0.92 -> 0.66
olivia: sounds like noisy neighbor on pool-3 is affecting cache locality. Can we add a headroom gauge that factors: usable_gpus * avg_batch_util - reserved_overhead? would make autoscaler decisions clearer
sachin: proposing a simple noisy-neighbor detector: sliding window p50/p95 divergence per-route, plus cross-route KV miss correlation. If divergence > 2x and correlation > 0.6 => flag
maria: added a text description on the dashboard for detector rules. Also included a small export of the profiler command we used:
```
# profiler snippet
profiler --pid $RUNTIME_PID --duration 60 --out /tmp/prof.json
python -m rl-perf analyze /tmp/prof.json --flamegraph | head -n 30
```
kevin: after pinning kernel selection thresholds in runtime (hotfix), I'm seeing p95 drop ~12% in canary. Will let it run another 20m and then roll to pool-3 if stable
olivia: please add a per-pool "cache warming" metric (recent unique prefixes warmed) so we can estimate transient cold starts after evictions
sachin: note: for Dedicated pools we should consider per-tenant KV namespaces to avoid cross-tenant thrash. That may require a config knob for private/dedicated only
maria: agree, added a TODO on the dash and flagged for the Dedicated capacity RFC. Filing a followup: https://go.redwood/issue/INF-847
kevin: thumbs up. once the roll is green I'll update the runbook to include the noisy-neighbor detector and remediation steps (evict small tenants, increase local kv size, or reserve headroom)
observability-bot: note: dashboard deployed to staging at 10:40 UTC, canary run started at 10:45 UTC
maria: thanks all — leaving the dashboard open in staging, will post final metrics in ~30m. :rocket:
